p: a way of settling a dispute in which an independent third party examines both sides' cases and makes a decision
that the two sides are usually bound to accept.
negotiation between employer representatives and employee representatives, usually a trade union,
to agree pay, hours and working conditions for a group of workers.
a procedure in which an independent third party helps employers and employees reach agreement
by encouraging discussion and suggesting compromises, without imposing a decision.
the involvement of workers in making decisions or shaping how the organisation operates,
ranging from being consulted to having a formal voice at board level.
collective measures taken by employees to put pressure on their employer in a dispute
which disrupt or restrict normal production or service.
a system that gives employees formal representation in how the business is governed,
so that decisions are shared with, rather than imposed on, the workforce.
the relationship between employers and employees or their representatives,
including how disputes, pay and working conditions are negotiated and resolved.
when an employer prevents employees from entering the workplace
to pressure them into accepting the employer's terms in a dispute.
a clause in an agreement in which employees or their union promise not to take strike action for a set period,
usually in return for agreed pay or conditions.
employees refusing to work any hours beyond their contracted hours
while carrying on with their normal hours, to pressure the employer in a dispute.
the loss of a job because the employer no longer needs the position,
not because of the employee's conduct or performance.
an agreement in which an employer recognises only one trade union to represent all its employees
in negotiations over pay and conditions.
a collective refusal by employees to carry out their work
to pressure an employer over a dispute.
an organisation of workers formed to represent their collective interests
by negotiating with employers over pay, conditions and job security.
employees carrying out only the duties set out in their contracts and following every rule strictly,
which slows output without a full strike.
